scope: Project-run cold-load mobile lab audit of the hosted app; three fresh Chrome profiles per route and release

configuration.cache: Fresh browser profile per run; Lighthouse storage reset enabled
configuration.aggregation: Median of 3 runs per metric, not one selected best run
configuration.reproduce: npm exec --yes --package lighthouse@13.5.0 -- node scripts/mobile-performance.mjs baseline; deploy candidate; repeat with final

changes: Load AI, graph and two-client route code only when that workspace is opened.
Start live admission records and WebSocket subscriptions only for verification views.
Render static pages before the artifact catalog loads.
Force production React and JSX output even when the calling shell exports NODE_ENV=development.
Verify historical session signatures in a dedicated worker; retain all checks and refuse worker errors/timeouts.
Defer the live two-client verifier until an actual request.
Preload the critical font, reserve loading space and keep mobile hero actions in stable rows.
Load the launch-video element and poster only after its disclosure is opened.
limitations: These are simulated mobile lab measurements on a Windows desktop, not tests on a physical low-end phone.
No field Core Web Vitals, real-user percentile or INP claim is made. TBT is a lab responsiveness proxy and is not INP.
Lighthouse scores and timings vary with desktop load, network, CDN and browser versions.
The two-client route verifies historical signed snapshots in a worker; cold-load latency is not solely an initial-bundle measurement.
This navigation audit does not measure the responsiveness of every later click or live verification request.

Lighthouse resource-summary undercounts dedicated-worker transfer in this Chrome run. Its byte fields are reported audit values; use the worker-free Overview route for the documented transfer comparison.
Main-thread paint/TBT metrics do not assert that background historical verification has finished at first paint.
